title: Introduce RAG offline-authoring sandbox with credentialed step-sim and policy-driven tool contracts
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add new offline-first RAG quickstart: authoring sandbox with credentialed step simulator, policy-driven tool contracts, and headless telemetry probes for reproducible e2e assertions.
description:
Context and motivation: Teams asked for a lightweight local-first authoring experience for RAG workflows that mirrors our hosted telemetry and policy semantics but works offline for training/evals and workshops. This quickstart provides a minimal sandbox CLI + browser dev UI that simulates credentialed tool calls, maintains a step-by-step session trace, and emits Redwood-format telemetry probes so teams can run offline e2e assertions against prompt/response traces.

What this PR adds: 1) quickstarts/rag-offline-sandbox/ with a small Node CLI (index.js) and a static React dev UI to step through sessions; 2) step-simulator that models credentialed tool calls and a policy-contract layer that enforces allowed parameter shapes; 3) a headless run mode for CI/eval that exports trace JSON compatible with existing telemetry ingest; 4) README with usage, authoring tips, and an assert-driven smoke harness for local reproducibility; 5) sample prompt sets and a verifier for response shape checks.

Checklist: - [x] implement step-simulator and tool-contract schema enforcement - [x] emit telemetry probes (session.start/session.step/session.end) - [x] provide headless runner + replayable trace export - [x] docs with quickstart steps and troubleshooting - [x] unit tests for contract validator and trace serializer - [x] basic e2e smoke in CI

Security and privacy notes: The sandbox runs entirely locally by default and includes a credential-mock that demonstrates token exchange but does not store secrets. The README includes explicit guidance for swapping in KMS-backed tokens for private deployments. Teams using the headless CI mode should ensure traces with secrets are scrubbed; the trace exporter includes a redaction flag.

How to try locally: 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/rag-offline-sandbox 2) yarn install && yarn start to open the dev UI 3) use the CLI via yarn run simulate --sample to generate a trace, then yarn run verify --trace=out.json to run assertions. The README contains troubleshooting tips for common environment issues (Node 18+, Yarn 1/2, and recommended Chrome).

Compatibility and scope: The quickstart intentionally keeps the runtime small (no GPU or Redwood runtime dependency) so it can be used in workshops and CI. Traces are emitted in a JSON shape that can be piped into Redwood's telemetry ingestion for downstream evals and alerts. This is not a production inference shim; it is an authoring/eval tool.

Related: references ENG-1289 for telemetry probe schema, PM-432 for workshop curriculum, and an internal doc link to the policy-contract design doc (linked in the README).
